## Look at Everything and its relationship to Perceived Visual Complexity

Analysis includes many tests for mean difference and statistical significance.

```{r, message=F}
library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
library(readr)
library(gtools)
library(janitor)
library(patchwork)
library(DT)
library(gt)
library(ggdist)
library(ggnewscale)

data <- read_csv("data/all_labeled_MASSVIS_5800.csv") %>% 
  clean_names()

data_agg <- tibble(
  label_group = NA, #i.e. source,multiplicity
  label = NA, # name of label, i.e. Area, Bar
  applies = NA,  # binary encoding, 0 = does not apply, 1 = applies
  n = NA, # count
  mean_complexity = NA,
  sd = NA,
  se = NA
)
```


# amount of each label in dataset

```{r}
amounts_data <- data %>% 
  select(-c(image_id,filename,news_category,science_category,infographic_category,government_category,panel_s,single_panel,multi_panel,amount_of_text, chart_types,category,chart_types_count,chart_count,color_count,quantitative,categorical))

amounts_data <- data.frame(t(colSums(amounts_data[,-1])))
           
write_csv(amounts_data,"data/amount_of_each_binary_label.csv")
```



```{r}
mean_comp <- data %>% 
  summarise(mean_comp = round(mean(mean_human_complexity_rating),2))

data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +
    geom_histogram(show.legend=F, color = "white",fill="gray50") +
    geom_vline(xintercept=mean_comp$mean_comp, color = "red",linewidth=1) +
    geom_text(x = (mean_comp$mean_comp + 5), y =310, label = mean_comp$mean_comp, color = "red") +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,100)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(
      x = "",
      y = ""
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      # axis.text = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      # panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
      # axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.5)
    ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")

# ggsave("figures_for_paper/complexity_distributions.png")
```







## Source

Run ANOVA — unequal sample sizes are not an assumption, but are something to consider when reading results.

``` {r}
category_aov = aov(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ category, data)
summary(category_aov)

```
Do Post-Hoc Tukey test

```{r}
tukey_test <- TukeyHSD(category_aov)
tukey_test

# get actual adjust p values
tukey_test$category[,"p adj"]

```


``` {r}
# temp <- tibble(category_f = factor(data$category, levels=c("Science","Infographic","News","Government")))
# data$category_f <- factor(data$category, levels=c("Science","Infographic","News","Government"))

data %>% 
    mutate(
    category = factor(category, labels=c("Government", "Infographic", "News", "Science"))
  ) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +
    geom_histogram(show.legend=F) +
    geom_point(data = cat_means, aes(x = mean_complexity, y = 0), color = "red", size = 3) +
    geom_vline(data = cat_means, aes(xintercept = mean_complexity), color = "red", size = 1, alpha = 0.75) +
    facet_wrap(~ factor(category, levels=c("Science","Infographic","News","Government")), ncol=1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,100),expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(
      x = "",
      y = ""
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      strip.text.x = element_blank()
      # axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.5)
    )
ggsave("figures_for_paper/category_distributions.png", width=4, height=8)

```



```{r}
data_agg <- cat_means %>% 
  mutate(applies=NA,
         label_group="Source") %>% 
  rename("label" = category) %>% 
  select(c(label_group,label,applies,everything()))

```

## Multiplicity

Do a t-test, first check if variance is different or not.

```{r}
panel_means <- data %>% 
  select(c(panel_s, mean_human_complexity_rating)) %>% 
  group_by(panel_s) %>% 
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_complexity = mean(mean_human_complexity_rating),
    sd = sd(mean_human_complexity_rating),
    se = sd / sqrt(n)
  )
panel_means
```

No significant variance difference

```{r}
data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +
    geom_histogram(show.legend=F) +
    geom_point(data = panel_means, aes(x = mean_complexity, y = 0), color = "red", size = 3) +
    geom_vline(data = panel_means, aes(xintercept = mean_complexity), color = "red", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~panel_s, ncol=1) +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,100),expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(
      x = "",
      y = ""
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      # axis.line.y = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.5)
    )

panels_ftest <- var.test(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ panel_s, data = data)
panels_ftest
```

Conduct the t-test

``` {r}

t.test(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ panel_s, data=data, var.equal=T)

```

```{r}
      x = "",
      y = ""
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      # axis.text = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
      # panel.border = element_rect(color = "gray50",
```

```{r}
panel_means <- panel_means %>% 
  mutate(applies=NA,

  rbind(panel_means)
```

## Text

A series of t-tests on the different text categories. Includes variance tests

### No text


```{r}
notext_means <- data %>% 
  select(c(no_text, mean_human_complexity_rating)) %>% 
  group_by(no_text) %>% 
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_complexity = mean(mean_human_complexity_rating),
    sd = sd(mean_human_complexity_rating),
    se = sd / sqrt(n)
  )
notext_means
```


```{r}
notext_agg <- notext_means %>% 
  mutate(label="no_text",
         label_group="Text") %>% 
  rename("applies" = "no_text") %>% 
  select(c(label_group,label,applies,everything()))

data_agg <- data_agg %>% 
  rbind(notext_agg)

```


No significant variance difference

```{r}
data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +
    geom_histogram() +
    facet_wrap(~no_text) +
    theme_minimal()

notext_ftest <- var.test(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ no_text, data = data)
notext_ftest
```

### Text-Only

```{r}
data %>% 
  select(c(text_only, mean_human_complexity_rating)) %>% 
  group_by(text_only) %>% 
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_complexity = mean(mean_human_complexity_rating),
    sd = sd(mean_human_complexity_rating),
    se = sd / sqrt(n)
  )
```



Significant variance difference

```{r}
data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +
    geom_histogram() +
    facet_wrap(~text_only) +
    theme_minimal()

textonly_ftest <- var.test(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ text_only, data = data)
textonly_ftest
```

Conduct the t-test

``` {r}
# variance is different — use welch t test
t.test(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ text_only, data=data, var.equal=F)

```

### Color Count

```{r}
cor.test(data$mean_human_complexity_rating, data$color_count, method = "pearson")
```


```{r}
data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = color_count, y = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_smooth(method="lm", se =T, color="#F99E77",fill="#F99E77") +
    theme_minimal() +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,100), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(
      x = "",
      y = ""
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.line = element_line(size=0.5,color="black"),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")


cor.test(data$mean_human_complexity_rating,data$color_count)
ggsave("figures_for_paper/scatters/colorcount_correlation.png", width=4, height=4)

```

```{r}
  ggplot(aes(x = chart_types_count, y = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +

    geom_smooth(method="lm", se =T, color="#A962CB",fill="#A962CB") +

      panel.grid = element_blank()
```

```{r}
    se = sd / sqrt(n)
  )
```

Significant variance difference

```{r}
data %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_human_complexity_rating)) +
    geom_histogram() +
    facet_wrap(~circle) +
    theme_minimal()

circle_ftest <- var.test(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ circle, data = data)
circle_ftest
```

Conduct the t-test

``` {r}

t.test(mean_human_complexity_rating ~ circle, data=data, var.equal=F)
```

# Aggregate Data

```{r}
data_agg %>% 
  filter(label_group == "Source") %>% 
  arrange(desc(mean_complexity))

data_agg %>% 
  filter(label_group == "Multiplicity") %>% 
  arrange(desc(mean_complexity))

# get higher mean values
data_agg %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Source") %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Multiplicity") %>% 
  group_by(label) %>% 
  slice_min(mean_complexity)
# get higher mean values — LABEL APPLIES
data_agg %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Source") %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Multiplicity") %>% 
  group_by(label) %>% 
  slice_max(mean_complexity) %>% 
  filter(applies == 1)

# get lower mean values
data_agg %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Source") %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Multiplicity") %>% 
  group_by(label) %>% 
  slice_min(mean_complexity)
# get higher mean values — LABEL APPLIES
data_agg %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Source") %>% 
  filter(label_group != "Multiplicity") %>% 
  group_by(label) %>% 
  slice_min(mean_complexity) %>% 
  filter(applies == 1)
  
```
